I am investigating the git history and `related_descriptors.py` / `query.py` to see how cached related objects are handled during `prefetch_related`.
I have resolved the issue in [django/db/models/fields/related_descriptors.py](file:///tmp/xhs-c6-host-cpni8g8b/django/db/models/fields/related_descriptors.py).

### Cause
When prefetching across a reverse one-to-one relation ([`ReverseOneToOneDescriptor.get_prefetch_queryset`](file:///tmp/xhs-c6-host-cpni8g8b/django/db/models/fields/related_descriptors.py#L366-L383)), forward one-to-one relation ([`ForwardManyToOneDescriptor.get_prefetch_queryset`](file:///tmp/xhs-c6-host-cpni8g8b/django/db/models/fields/related_descriptors.py#L120-L150)), or reverse many-to-one relation ([`RelatedManager.get_prefetch_queryset`](file:///tmp/xhs-c6-host-cpni8g8b/django/db/models/fields/related_descriptors.py#L635-L655)), iterating over `queryset` evaluates the inner queryset (including its nested `prefetch_related` lookups) and then unconditionally sets the reverse relation cache on each `rel_obj` to the outer `instance`. This overwrote the inner prefetched object on `rel_obj` with the outer `instance` (which had different deferred fields).

### Solution
Updated `get_prefetch_queryset()` in [`ForwardManyToOneDescriptor`](file:///tmp/xhs-c6-host-cpni8g8b/django/db/models/fields/related_descriptors.py#L145-L149), [`ReverseOneToOneDescriptor`](file:///tmp/xhs-c6-host-cpni8g8b/django/db/models/fields/related_descriptors.py#L379-L382), and [`RelatedManager`](file:///tmp/xhs-c6-host-cpni8g8b/django/db/models/fields/related_descriptors.py#L650-L653) to only populate the reverse relation cache on `rel_obj` if it is not already cached.
